input.summary:
P2 back bedroom furnished in parts/room-17.mjs: two yellow beds (west wall at x28, east wall with the head at x33), a two-barrel dresser on the back wall with a standing lantern and a flower pot, and a hanging lantern over the lane.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with 8 blocks placed for this part, no REFUSED or off-palette writes. The room check says OK, 12 of 12 cells reachable and min light 9, when walked from inside the room (entrance at (29,8,14)).
Bed 2 is moved from the planned x33 heads-south spot to foot (32,8,15) with its head at (33,8,15) against the east wall, because its foot at (33,8,14) would hang over the stair hole. Recorded in plan.md's Notes.

waste.what: Worked out bed and lane cells by hand, checking each against the stair hole, rail, door and the bed-reachability rule (a bed must have a standable neighbour).
waste.cost: about 6 minutes of reasoning and 3 check runs
waste.tool: A `mcd plan` option that marks stair holes, rails and bed-reachable neighbour cells, or a bed-placement dry run that reports the reachable side of each bed.

waste.what: Walk verdict shows 0 of 12 reachable while the front bedroom and door are still stubs, so I wrote a temp rooms.json with the entrance moved into my room to test internal walkability.
waste.cost: 1 extra node script and 2 check runs
waste.tool: `mcd room --entrance x,y,z` (or a per-room mode that walks from the room's own door cell) so a room can be verified before its neighbours are built.

waste.what: hanging_lantern silently returns 0 when no solid block is within 4 cells above, and the stub roof here isn't built, so the hanging lantern placed nothing in this copy. I found this only by probing cells.
waste.cost: 1 probe script, 1 run
waste.tool: A warning from hanging_lantern (or `mcd room`) when a requested lantern is not placed, plus a check for the roof-dependent placement.

waste.what: Probed single cells with a throwaway script to see what was in the build, because the room tool does not show block contents above the floor.
waste.cost: 1 script
waste.tool: `mcd zoom` or a `mcd cell x,y,z` query for a short list of cells.

companions.task: Confirm the stair hole at (33,7,14) and rail at (32,8,14) and that they line up with the bed and lane I chose, so the bed foot at (32,8,15) and the lane at (31,14) stay clear of their flight.
Check the hanging lantern at (31,10,14) once the roof part exists, and whether a second light is needed by the window end of the room.

left: Only 2 of the 4 upstairs beds are built here (back bedroom); the other two are the P2 front bedroom's (part 15).

Bed 2 moved from the planned head-at-x33-south to foot (32,8,15), head (33,8,15) facing east, to keep clear of the stair hole at (33,7,14). Recorded in plan.md Notes; the plan's bed list still shows the old spot.

The hanging lantern at (31,10,14) places nothing until the roof part puts a solid block within 4 cells above it; it is 0 here because the roof is not built in this copy. The standing lantern on the dresser alone already gives min light 9.
Walk from the house entrance is unverified until the front bedroom and its door are built; from inside the room, all 12 cells are reachable.
`mcd check` reports floating and unsupported blocks in other parts (stairs at 54/88/91, ladders at 62 and 78); none are in my box and I did not touch them.

input.summary:
P0 east front room furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: cyan bed (foot 8,3,12, head 9,3,12 to the east wall), spruce table (fence leg + top slab, lantern on top) at 9,10 under the front window, a stair chair at 8,10, and a hanging lantern over the aisle at 8,11. Lane x7 z10..12 kept clear from the front door to the partition door.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; this part places 6 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. Room check: light min 9, 0 dark cells, FIT OK for this room.
Walk check still says UNREACHABLE because the shell's door and walls are not built yet in this copy; the hanging lantern places nothing until a ceiling exists.
left: WALK verdict is UNREACHABLE only because the front door (7,3..4,9) and the walls are stubs in this copy; re-run `mcd room` once shell_a is in, and confirm the lane x7 z10..12 is reachable from the door.
hanging_lantern(8,6,11) places nothing while the roof/ceiling cell above is air; it needs the roof part built first (check after the merge). The standing lantern on the table alone gives light min 9.
Not ticked in elements.md: its 'Every room lit' item is whole-site and this room is only one of 46. Plan.md has no per-part checklist.
The table is a 2-high fence + top slab (surface y5), to keep nothing on a bottom slab; a lower bottom-slab table would need a different surface.
No carpet: palette.json has no carpet id, so no rug. The room has no dresser or shelf: a 3x3 room with a 2-cell bed leaves no free wall cell that keeps the lane clear.

waste.what: Worked out each cell of the 3x3 room (bed, table, chair, lane, aisle) by hand from the plan grid instead of reading a generated layout
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of reasoning on coordinates and clearances
waste.tool: `mcd plan --only` could print a candidate layout (furniture footprints plus the lane check) so it can be tested before writing the module

waste.what: Walk verdict cannot be used before the shell exists: `mcd room` reports 0 of 9 cells reachable because the door is a stub
waste.cost: one extra build and check cycle to tell a real unreachable cell from a missing door
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-doors` (or treating the planned door cells as open) so the furnisher can check lanes against the planned doors before the shell is built

waste.what: Hanging lanterns depend on a ceiling that the roof part provides later, so the helper places nothing in an isolated check
waste.cost: one rebuild to see the lantern was skipped
waste.tool: `hanging_lantern` should report the skip reason (no ceiling in reach) in its return value so the furnisher can see it at once

companions.task: Confirm the roof cell above the aisle at (8,7,11) is solid so the hanging lantern at (8,6,11) hangs from it, and that the cells over the bed stay clear of the eave.
